commands.name: skill:principle-attack-the-premise
commands.description: Apply when two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Write the premise down and test it directly before you write another fix that assumes it.

commands.name: skill:principle-boundary-discipline
commands.description: Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.

commands.name: skill:principle-build-the-lever
commands.description: Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun.

commands.name: skill:principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
commands.description: Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction. Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.

commands.name: skill:principle-exhaust-the-design-space
commands.description: Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.

commands.name: skill:principle-experience-first
commands.description: Apply when product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs come up. Choose user delight over implementation convenience; ship fewer polished features over more rough ones.

commands.name: skill:principle-explain-the-number
commands.description: Apply before you measure, and before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result. Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.

commands.name: skill:principle-fix-root-causes
commands.description: Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate.

commands.name: skill:principle-foundational-thinking
commands.description: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.

commands.name: skill:principle-guard-the-context-window
commands.description: Apply when context is filling up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads.

commands.name: skill:principle-laziness-protocol
commands.description: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.

commands.name: skill:principle-make-operations-idempotent
commands.description: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.

commands.name: skill:principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
commands.description: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.

commands.name: skill:principle-minimize-reader-load
commands.description: Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope.

commands.name: skill:principle-model-the-domain
commands.description: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files.

commands.name: skill:principle-never-block-on-the-human
commands.description: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work.

commands.name: skill:principle-outcome-oriented-execution
commands.description: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code.

commands.name: skill:principle-prove-it-works
commands.description: Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'

commands.name: skill:principle-redesign-from-first-principles
commands.description: Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design.

commands.name: skill:principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
commands.description: Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object. Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant.

commands.name: skill:principle-sequence-verifiable-units
commands.description: Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer.

commands.name: skill:principle-subtract-before-you-add
commands.description: Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead code, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base.

commands.name: skill:principle-test-behavior-not-implementation
commands.description: Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Assert what the code's users can observe, so that the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change.

commands.name: skill:principle-type-system-discipline
commands.description: Apply when designing types, reviewing a function signature, or writing code in any statically-typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, exhaust variants, derive from authoritative schemas.

commands.name: skill:principle-attack-the-premise
commands.description: Apply when two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Write the premise down and test it directly before you write another fix that assumes it.

commands.name: skill:principle-boundary-discipline
commands.description: Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.

commands.name: skill:principle-build-the-lever
commands.description: Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun.

commands.name: skill:principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
commands.description: Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction. Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.

commands.name: skill:principle-exhaust-the-design-space
commands.description: Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.

commands.name: skill:principle-experience-first
commands.description: Apply when product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs come up. Choose user delight over implementation convenience; ship fewer polished features over more rough ones.

commands.name: skill:principle-explain-the-number
commands.description: Apply before you measure, and before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result. Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.

commands.name: skill:principle-fix-root-causes
commands.description: Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate.

commands.name: skill:principle-foundational-thinking
commands.description: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.

commands.name: skill:principle-guard-the-context-window
commands.description: Apply when context is filling up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads.

commands.name: skill:principle-laziness-protocol
commands.description: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.

commands.name: skill:principle-make-operations-idempotent
commands.description: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.

commands.name: skill:principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
commands.description: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.

commands.name: skill:principle-minimize-reader-load
commands.description: Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope.

commands.name: skill:principle-model-the-domain
commands.description: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files.

commands.name: skill:principle-never-block-on-the-human
commands.description: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work.

commands.name: skill:principle-outcome-oriented-execution
commands.description: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code.

commands.name: skill:principle-prove-it-works
commands.description: Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'

commands.name: skill:principle-redesign-from-first-principles
commands.description: Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design.

commands.name: skill:principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
commands.description: Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object. Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant.

commands.name: skill:principle-sequence-verifiable-units
commands.description: Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer.

commands.name: skill:principle-subtract-before-you-add
commands.description: Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead code, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base.

commands.name: skill:principle-test-behavior-not-implementation
commands.description: Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Assert what the code's users can observe, so that the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change.

commands.name: skill:principle-type-system-discipline
commands.description: Apply when designing types, reviewing a function signature, or writing code in any statically-typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, exhaust variants, derive from authoritative schemas.

commands.name: skill:qmd

commands.description: Apply before you measure, and before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result. Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.

commands.name: skill:principle-fix-root-causes
commands.description: Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate.

commands.name: skill:principle-foundational-thinking
commands.description: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.

commands.name: skill:principle-guard-the-context-window
commands.description: Apply when context is filling up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads.

commands.name: skill:principle-laziness-protocol
commands.description: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.

commands.name: skill:principle-make-operations-idempotent
commands.description: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.

commands.name: skill:principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
commands.description: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.

commands.name: skill:principle-minimize-reader-load
commands.description: Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope.

commands.name: skill:principle-model-the-domain
commands.description: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files.

commands.name: skill:principle-never-block-on-the-human
commands.description: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work.

commands.name: skill:principle-outcome-oriented-execution
commands.description: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code.

commands.name: skill:principle-prove-it-works
commands.description: Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'

commands.name: skill:principle-redesign-from-first-principles
commands.description: Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design.

commands.name: skill:principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
commands.description: Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object. Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant.

commands.name: skill:principle-sequence-verifiable-units
commands.description: Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer.

commands.name: skill:principle-subtract-before-you-add
commands.description: Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead code, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base.

commands.name: skill:principle-test-behavior-not-implementation
commands.description: Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Assert what the code's users can observe, so that the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change.

commands.name: skill:principle-type-system-discipline
commands.description: Apply when designing types, reviewing a function signature, or writing code in any statically-typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, exhaust variants, derive from authoritative schemas.

commands.name: skill:qmd
commands.description: Search local markdown knowledge bases, notes, docs, and wikis with QMD. Use when users ask to find notes, retrieve documents, inspect a wiki, answer from indexed markdown, or set up QMD access.

commands.name: skill:recall
commands.description: Reconstruct your recent working context from your own chat history, live state, and the shared record (user reports, prior fixes, incidents), then hand back a tight current-state brief. Use for 'recall my work on X', 'catch me up', 'what have I been working on', 'where did I leave off', before starting or resuming work.

commands.name: skill:reflect
commands.description: Spawn three parallel review subagents over the active transcript, surface learnings, and route each to a concrete edit on an existing skill. Use when the user says reflect.

commands.name: skill:rex
commands.description: Use the rex CLI to manage Rex sessions, open tabs, arrange panes, run commands, inspect terminal output, and control connected Rex apps.

commands.name: skill:rust-design-patterns
commands.description: Resolve Rust ownership and lifetime problems or design Rust APIs, resource lifecycles, and FFI boundaries.

commands.name: skill:rust-expert
commands.description: Expert Rust guidelines covering ownership, error handling, async patterns, API design, memory optimization, performance, testing, and anti-patterns. Trigger when the user is writing or reviewing Rust (.rs files, Cargo.toml), designing library APIs or builder types, asking about error handling with thiserror/anyhow, async code with tokio, HashMap/collection patterns, or Cargo workspace and release profile configuration. Also trigger for clippy warnings, borrow checker questions, or any request to review Rust code for idioms and best practices. Do NOT trigger when the question is specifically about Leptos (use the leptos skill), LadybugDB (use the ladybug skill), or Restate (use the restate skill) — even if Rust code is involved.

commands.name: skill:rust-face-config-confique
commands.description: Use when designing or writing config loading (CLI flags, env vars, config files) for a Rust binary/face in the user's repos (alvin, tin, crumbs).

commands.name: skill:scaffolding-gpui-kit-app
commands.description: Scaffold a new GPUI Kit desktop Rust app: workspace manifest, crate shape, startup sequence, headless test, and Debug profile overrides; includes testing views backed by external (tokio) services.

commands.name: skill:security-and-hardening
commands.description: Hardens code against vulnerabilities. Use when auditing an input handler for vulnerabilities, when handling user input, authentication, data storage, or external integrations, or when checking a login flow is safe against the OWASP Top Ten. Use when building any feature that accepts untrusted data, manages user sessions, or interacts with third-party services. Use when auditing dependencies for known vulnerabilities, triaging package-manager audit findings, or assessing supply-chain risk in a new package. Use when personal data or privacy compliance (GDPR, CCPA) is involved.

commands.name: skill:seed-rust-agents
commands.description: Use when starting a new Rust project or repo in this family, or when an existing Rust repo lacks agent docs. Seeds AGENTS.md, the rust-review command, mise tasks, and hk config from the family templates. Triggers on: "new rust project", "seed agents", "set up agent docs", "add AGENTS.md", greenfield Rust repos. Ask for project specifics, then write the files.

commands.name: skill:sharpen
commands.description: Make a task deeper, not bigger, then rewrite the prompt. Use for /sharpen.

commands.name: skill:shipping-and-launch
commands.description: Prepares production launches. Use when preparing to deploy to production, or when asking what needs to be in place before shipping. Use when you need a pre-launch checklist, when setting up monitoring, when planning a staged rollout, or when you need a rollback strategy.

commands.name: skill:show-me-your-work
commands.description: Keep a reviewable decision trail for long-running or unattended work: a TSV log with one row per decision (what, why, evidence, result). Local by default; commit it when a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result. Use for /show-me-your-work, autonomous or multi-phase runs, or work a human reviews after stepping away.

commands.name: skill:source-driven-development
commands.description: Grounds every implementation decision in official documentation. Use when you want to verify an approach against the official docs before implementing it, or when you want authoritative, source-cited code free from outdated patterns. Use when building with any framework or library where correctness matters.

commands.name: skill:spec-driven-development
commands.description: Creates specs before coding. Use when starting a new project, feature, or significant change and no specification exists yet. Use when drafting a PRD or requirements document with objectives and scope, or when requirements are unclear, ambiguous, or only exist as a vague idea. Use when a single requirement spans several independently testable capabilities and needs decomposing into a capability map of modules before specifying.

commands.name: skill:statechart
commands.description: Check a TLA+ model of a system that moves between states, such as a product flow, a protocol, or a service, and draw it as a Mermaid statechart. The report gives the shortest path to each state that breaks a rule. Use for /statechart, or to show a bug as a path through states.

commands.name: skill:swarm
commands.description: Fan out N parallel workers, drain them, and return one report. Use for /swarm, 'swarm this', or parallel coverage, races, gauntlets, and exploration.

commands.name: skill:taming-ai
commands.description: (no description)

commands.name: skill:tavily-best-practices
commands.description: Build production-ready Tavily integrations with best practices baked in. Reference documentation for developers using coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) to implement web search, content extraction, crawling, and research in agentic workflows, RAG systems, or autonomous agents.

commands.name: skill:tavily-research
commands.description: Research a topic in depth with Tavily. Use this skill when a question needs many sources gathered and weighed together: analysing a market, policy, technology or trend, comparing options across several criteria, reviewing the literature, or any request to research, investigate or analyze something in depth. A single fact or answer to find, even one with many clues, is a tavily-search task. For one CRM record use tavily-entity, for a table of matches use tavily-list, and for a recurring check use tavily-monitor.

commands.name: skill:tavily-search
commands.description: Use this skill whenever a task needs the web: searching for information, checking current facts or news, finding sources, reading a URL, finding a page on a site, or collecting many pages from a site. Use it for anything past your training data or anything the user wants verified online.

commands.name: skill:tdd
commands.description: Use only when the user explicitly asks for TDD, a failing test, or a regression test, OR when the bug has an obvious cheap local test target. Skip when the test path is unclear, expensive, integration-heavy, or not requested.

commands.name: skill:teach
commands.description: Explain a body of work plainly so a person actually understands it. Runs the `how` and `why` skills and weaves what they find into one clear explanation. Use for 'teach me this', 'help me really understand X', 'explain this change or subsystem to me'.

commands.name: skill:technical-writing
commands.description: Layered technical-writing standard: Diátaxis structure, Google developer style sentences, STE instruction rules, Global English syntax. Use for /skill:technical-writing or when writing or reviewing docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages.

commands.name: skill:tern-agent-halt-watch
commands.description: Build a Tern polling watch that parses an agent's approval prompt in a terminal pane, auto-answers the expected cases, and only alerts on the rest

commands.name: skill:tern-carly-pane-watch
commands.description: Build a tern.carly.schedule polling watch that parses an agent/shell pane's screen and either auto-answers the agent or alerts the user

commands.name: skill:tern-plugin-authoring
commands.description: Author, validate or debug a Tern plugin (plugin.toml + host.luau/window.luau), including offline schema validation without touching the live app.

commands.name: skill:tern-remote-mobile-pairing
commands.description: Authorize a phone's Tern device key on a headless remote host when tern remote doctor says FAIL key … not in authorized_keys.

commands.name: skill:test-driven-development
commands.description: Drives development with tests using the red-green-refactor loop. Use when implementing any logic, fixing any bug, or changing any behavior. Use when you need to prove that code works, when a bug report arrives, or when you're about to modify existing functionality. Use when asked to add tests to a function, fix a bug in it or change its behavior, even when the code is pasted inline and the request does not mention tests.

commands.name: skill:typescript-best-practices
commands.description: TypeScript best practices. Use when reading or editing any .ts or .tsx file.

commands.name: skill:typescript-vertical-monolith
commands.description: Enforce vertical-slice modular monolith architecture for TypeScript. Activate when: creating/refactoring features, designing architecture, adding modules, structuring backends, or when drift toward hexagonal/clean-architecture/DDD/repository-interfaces is likely. Trigger phrases: "vertical slices", "modular monolith", "feature structure", "keep it concrete", "don't over-architect".

commands.name: skill:unslop
commands.description: Cut AI tells from any writing.

commands.name: skill:using-agent-skills
commands.description: Discovers and invokes agent skills. Use when starting a session, or when you need to decide which skill or workflow applies to the piece of work at hand. This is the meta-skill that governs how all other skills are discovered and invoked.

commands.name: skill:verify-against-a-spec-suite-you-are-writing
commands.description: Use when rewriting a core crate's model while tests for the new model are being authored separately, to harvest real defects instead of shipping a self-consistent wrong model

commands.name: skill:web-perf
commands.description: Audit, diagnose, or optimize website loading and interaction performance, Core Web Vitals, and Lighthouse performance scores.

commands.name: skill:why
commands.description: Use for 'why does X work this way', 'why we picked Y', design rationale, regressions, postmortems, or data-backed thresholds. Discovers available MCPs and queries each evidence category (source control, issue tracker, long-form docs, real-time chat, infrastructure observability, error tracking, product analytics warehouse) in parallel, then returns a cited read on decisions and tradeoffs. Use how for runtime behavior.

commands.name: skill:workers-best-practices
commands.description: Cloudflare Workers best practices for production applications. Use when writing, reviewing, or configuring Workers.

commands.name: skill:wrangler
commands.description: Run or troubleshoot Wrangler CLI commands in projects that have a wrangler.jsonc, wrangler.json, or wrangler.toml file, including local development, Previews, deployment, and resource management. For new projects and projects without a Wrangler configuration file, use the cf CLI instead.

commands.name: skill:write-rust
commands.description: Use when writing, refactoring, or reviewing Rust in this repo family: new functions or modules, fallible APIs, error types, builders, async or streaming code, trait and type design, dependency placement, or module structure. Triggers on: .rs files, Cargo.toml changes, borrow checker or clippy questions, API-shape questions, pre-review authoring checks. Pure idioms defer to rust-design-patterns and rust-expert; the repo's AGENTS.md wins on conflict.

commands.name: skill:writing-documentation-with-diataxis
commands.description: Applies the Diataxis framework to create or improve technical documentation. Use when being asked to write high quality tutorials, how-to guides, reference docs, or explanations, when reviewing documentation quality, or when deciding what type of documentation to create. Helps identify documentation types using the action/cognition and acquisition/application dimensions.
